fixes.explanation: The Amorites aren't the ones the Canaanites name, baker. They see the mourning at Atad and say, “This is a solemn ceremony of mourning by the Egyptians.” (Genesis 50:11). The text says that's how the place across the Jordan came to be called Abel-mizraim. So the answer was in what the Canaanites said, and no Amorites showed up to the ceremony.

Leaving isn't what he says, friend. The brothers come bowing low, saying, “We are your slaves!” (Genesis 50:18), and his first words are, “Do not be afraid.” (Genesis 50:19). Then he tells them, “I will provide for you and your little ones.” (Genesis 50:21). Nobody gets a “pack your bags” speech there. The text says he reassured his brothers and spoke kindly to them.

problems.problem: The explanation suggests that the Egyptian elders and chariots are why the Canaanites called it an Egyptian ceremony. The text does not say why they called it that.
Joseph promises to provide for his brothers and their little ones, but the text does not say he is keeping them close.
